Rus people contesting property or debt sought witnesses, sureties and a competent authority. Oaths carried religious weight, and access to credible supporters shaped disputes. While awaiting judgment, land, goods and household work still needed attention. Enforcers identified parties, disputed property and authority. Escort and custody consumed people, and excessive force could turn compensation claims into new injury and retaliation.
